subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call-threshold behavior be exposed to workspace/internal hooks, kept in typed plugin hooks, or split between those two surfaces?
rationale: The missing surface is source-reproducible, but the safe payload, authority, ordering, and threshold semantics require maintainer API and security-boundary intent.

options.title: Stage observation-only internal hooks
options.body: Add narrow workspace/internal observation events for subagent and turn completion with safe payloads, while leaving mutation and mid-turn control in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Keep lifecycle hooks plugin-only
options.body: Treat existing typed plugin hooks as the supported lifecycle surface and narrow this request away from workspace hooks that need sensitive run data.

options.title: Design one lifecycle contract first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a combined internal/plugin lifecycle model, payload shape, and threshold configuration semantics.

recommendation.title: Stage observation-only internal hooks
recommendation.body: Add narrow workspace/internal observation events for subagent and turn completion with safe payloads, while leaving mutation and mid-turn control in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is centered on typed plugin hook contracts and lifecycle/security boundaries where recent related PRs and source history point.
